causal_diagnosis: The policy learns to do nothing (action 0) 85% of the time, leading to uncontrolled descent and crash. The progress shaping (-1*distance -0.3*|vy|) is strongly negative, but the crash penalty (-100) dominates, so the agent cannot find a better policy. The success bonus is never reached because the agent never attempts to land properly. The previous edit (reducing progress shaping and adding main engine reward) failed because it did not address the core issue: the agent needs a strong, immediate positive signal for using the main engine to descend, not just a small bonus.
component_interaction_diagnosis: The crash penalty (-100) and progress shaping (-91.6) together create a large negative return that overwhelms any positive signal. The agent receives -100 for crashing and -91.6 for moving away from the pad, but no positive reward for using the main engine to descend. The main engine reward added in the previous edit (+0.5) was too weak to overcome the negative shaping. The agent needs a much stronger incentive to fire the main engine and descend toward the pad.
failed_pattern_reuse_check: The previous edit (medium scope) added a main engine reward of +0.5 but it was too weak. This revision will increase the main engine reward significantly and also add a positive reward for reducing vertical speed (vy) when the main engine is firing, to directly encourage controlled descent. We will not reduce progress shaping further because it already provides useful gradient; instead we will add a strong positive counterbalance.

search_decision.reason: The policy is stuck in a local optimum of doing nothing and crashing. We need to add a strong positive reward for using the main engine (action 2) to descend, and also reward reducing vertical speed when the engine is on. This is a medium edit because we are adding two new terms but keeping the overall structure.
